transcript.text: The sides of our new fridge freezer get really warm, almost hot, especially near the front edge. Is that a fire risk? It's in an alcove between two units.

It is very unlikely to be a fire risk. Modern fridge-freezers dissipate heat through coils (condensers) located in the sides or rear; feeling warm sides is normal operation as it moves heat away from your food. However, because yours is new and tucked into an alcove, it might not have enough airflow to shed that heat efficiently, which can make the sides feel hotter than usual. Please check two things: first, ensure there are at least a few centimetres of gap around the back and sides for air to circulate (if it's pressed tight against wood, heat builds up). If it’s running but feels extremely hot with no airflow, we need to check if the ventilation is blocked.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
Thanks. There's about 1cm gap each side, and a few cm gap above under the cupboard. No burning smell or scorch marks, and nothing has tripped. Is that enough room?

One centimetre is not enough for proper airflow. Manufacturers typically recommend at least 5cm (2 inches) of clearance on the sides and back so heat can escape freely; with only 1cm, the warm air gets trapped against the cabinet walls, making them feel very hot. This is probably normal operation, not a fault or fire risk. The compressor works harder to push heat out through those side panels, and without space for that heat to dissipate, the sides become much hotter than they would be in an open room. To fix this safely: pull the fridge-freezer out slightly (even just 4-5cm) to create a gap at the back and sides, ensuring nothing blocks the airflow behind it. If you can't move it further, check that the grille at the bottom front isn't blocked by carpet or debris. As long as there are no burning smells, scorch marks, or tripped fuses (which you've confirmed), this is safe to run once you improve the ventilation. It may take a day or two for the sides to cool down noticeably after creating that gap.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I'd rather not pull it out, we've just had new flooring laid and I'm worried about scratching it. Is there anything else I can do without moving it? The manual says to leave space but I didn't check exactly how much.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Focus on ensuring nothing blocks the air intake at the bottom or back. Check that the grille at the very base (front) is not covered by carpet, rugs, or debris, and ensure there are no items stored directly behind it blocking the rear ventilation. You can also gently vacuum the front grille to remove any dust buildup that might be restricting airflow.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

Ok. I can't see the bottom grille being blocked by anything, and there's nothing behind it that I know of since I can't see back there. Is it still okay to leave it running while I do this, or should I really unplug it first? I'd rather not lose the food if I don't need to.

You can leave it running; unplugging it is not necessary and risks food spoilage. The warmth you feel is the fridge doing its job of moving heat out through the side panels. The remaining factor is the tight 1cm gap on the sides. While this isn't a fire risk (no burning smell or tripping), it does mean the appliance has to work harder because the heat gets trapped against the cabinet walls rather than dissipating into the room. Just ensure the front grille remains clear of dust and carpet fibres, which is the only maintenance step you can safely perform from the current position.
